culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Standards of dress and behaviour are conservative in the Kyrgyz Republic. Take care not to offend. If in doubt, dress modestly and seek local advice. Obvious displays of affection, even between married couples, can offend. Police may harass or detain you. Same-sex relationships are legal in the Kyrgyz Republic but aren't widely accepted. Ramadan: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in the Kyrgyz Republic. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking, and smoking may be illegal in public during the day. If you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan. The Kyrgyz Ministry of Foreign Affairs' tourism pages describe nomadic hospitality. Accept tea, remove shoes in homes and yurts, and ask before photographing people.
culture-and-protocol.note: Read from the Australian Government's description of local customs.
